title: Gauged: With Lagged Streamflow Inputs
subtitle: 531 basins — Models ingesting lagged observed streamflow Q(t-1), autoregression, or data assimilation.

rows.family_description: Regional 256-unit LSTM networks ingesting 1-day-lagged observed streamflow Q(t-1) via scheduled-sampling autoregression with Bernoulli Markov observation holdout (AR-LSTM: no holdout and 0.5 holdout) or test-time 5-day sliding-window variational cell-state data assimilation (DA-LSTM) across 531 CAMELS-US basins forced by Daymet, Maurer, and NLDAS.
rows.notes: Autoregression LSTM without observation holdout during training (f_train = 0.0, f_test = 0.0, 1-day lead time) from Nearing et al. (2022, HESS 26, 5493-5513, Table 2, p. 5497; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7063252). Trained on 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 and evaluated on 1989-10-01 to 1999-09-30 across 531 CAMELS-US basins forced by Daymet, Maurer, and NLDAS + Q(t-1).

rows.family_description: Regional 256-unit LSTM networks ingesting 1-day-lagged observed streamflow Q(t-1) via scheduled-sampling autoregression with Bernoulli Markov observation holdout (AR-LSTM: no holdout and 0.5 holdout) or test-time 5-day sliding-window variational cell-state data assimilation (DA-LSTM) across 531 CAMELS-US basins forced by Daymet, Maurer, and NLDAS.
rows.notes: Autoregression LSTM with 50% Bernoulli Markov observation holdout during training (f_train = 0.5, mean missing sequence length = 5 days, f_test = 0.0, 1-day lead time) from Nearing et al. (2022, HESS 26, 5493-5513, Table 2, p. 5497; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7063252). Trained on 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 and evaluated on 1989-10-01 to 1999-09-30 across 531 CAMELS-US basins forced by Daymet, Maurer, and NLDAS + Q(t-1).

rows.family_description: Regional 256-unit LSTM networks ingesting 1-day-lagged observed streamflow Q(t-1) via scheduled-sampling autoregression with Bernoulli Markov observation holdout (AR-LSTM: no holdout and 0.5 holdout) or test-time 5-day sliding-window variational cell-state data assimilation (DA-LSTM) across 531 CAMELS-US basins forced by Daymet, Maurer, and NLDAS.
rows.notes: Unregularized Variational Data Assimilation LSTM (alpha_c = 0, alpha_y = 1, 5-day assimilation window [t-5, t-1], 1-day lead time) on a frozen regional LSTM from Nearing et al. (2022, HESS 26, 5493-5513, Table 2, p. 5497; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7063252). rows.family_description: Encoder-decoder Transformer (RR-Former; d_model=64, 4 attention heads, num_encoder_layers=1, num_decoder_layers=1, dim_feedforward=256, 3-layer MLP head 64->32->16->1 with LeakyReLU) ingesting 7-day meteorological forcing sequences, 27 static catchment attributes, and 7-day lagged observed streamflow Q(t-7..t-1), trained via 300-epoch regional pretraining across all 531 CAMELS-US basins followed by 40-epoch per-basin fine-tuning at lr=1e-4 with early stopping (Yin et al., 2022; iThronne/RR-Former).
rows.notes: Yin et al. (2022) RR-Former (d_model=64, nhead=4, num_encoder_layers=1, num_decoder_layers=1, dim_feedforward=256, 7-day lookback, 3-layer MLP head 64->32->16->1) trained via 300-epoch regional pretraining across all 531 CAMELS-US basins over WY1999-2008 followed by 40-epoch per-basin fine-tuning (lr=1e-4, patience=10), evaluated over WY1989-1999 with Daymet + 7-day lagged streamflow Q(t-7..t-1); 3-seed ensemble mean (seeds 601, 602, 603; Ensemble Med NSE = 0.847, Mean NSE = 0.822, Med KGE = 0.862, NSE <= 0 = 0).

rows.paradigm: Data-Integration LSTM with 1-Day Lagged Streamflow Q(t-1)
rows.asterisk_reason: Evaluated on WY1991–1999 (9 water years; 1989–1990 used as spin-up) as reported by Jamaat et al. (2025) for the Feng et al. (2020) DI(1)-LSTM benchmark.
rows.family_description: Regional 256-unit Long Short-Term Memory network with 1-day lagged observed specific discharge Q(t-1) data integration (DI(1)-LSTM; Feng et al., 2020, mhpi/hydroDL), trained on 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 and evaluated on WY1991–1999 (9 water years; 1989–1990 used as 365-day spin-up buffer) across the 531 Newman CAMELS-US basins with Daymet forcing as reported by Jamaat et al. (2025, Table 1).
rows.notes: Original mhpi/hydroDL DI(1)-LSTM (Feng et al., 2020; single model, hidden_size=256, seq_len=365, batch_size=100, dropout=0.5, 100 epochs, Eq. 11 log-sqrt transform log10(sqrt(v)+0.1)) trained on 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 across the 531 Newman CAMELS-US basins with Daymet forcing + 1-day lagged observed streamflow Q(t-1) and evaluated on WY1991–1999 (1990-10-01 to 1999-09-30, with 1989–1990 used as 365-day spin-up buffer), as reported in Jamaat et al. (2025, Journal of Hydrology 663, 134137, Table 1, p. 15; previously indexed as t5_09 in gauged__lagged_streamflow.json): Median NSE = 0.84, Median KGE = 0.855, Low-flow RMSE = 0.04 mm/d, High-flow RMSE = 2.83 mm/d.

(2022) RR-Former (d_model=64, nhead=4, num_encoder_layers=1, num_decoder_layers=1, dim_feedforward=256, 7-day lookback, 3-layer MLP head 64->32->16->1) trained via 300-epoch regional pretraining across all 531 CAMELS-US basins over WY1999-2008 followed by 40-epoch per-basin fine-tuning (lr=1e-4, patience=10), evaluated over WY1989-1999 with Daymet + 7-day lagged streamflow Q(t-7..t-1); single-model performance averaged across all 3 random seeds (seeds 601, 602, 603; evaluation_mode='single_member_mean'; Single-Seed Med NSE = 0.839 ± 0.002).

rows.paradigm: Differentiable HBV (δHBV 1.1p) + 5-Day Variational State & Precip DA
rows.asterisk_reason: Evaluated on WY1991–1999 (9 water years; 1989–1990 used as 365-day spin-up buffer) in Jamaat et al. (2025).
rows.family_description: 16-bucket differentiable HBV (δHBV 1.1p, with 3 dynamic time-varying parameters predicted by a 256-unit regional LSTM from 3 Daymet meteorological forcings and 35 static catchment attributes) coupled with training-free 5-day sliding-window variational data assimilation (Adadelta, 5 steps per window, NSELossBatch3 with monotonic acceptance gating) that updates initial hydrological log-states (SNOWPACK, MELTWATER, SM, SUZ, SLZ; δHBV-DA-S), last-day precipitation multiplier k^4 (δHBV-DA-P), or both jointly (δHBV-DA-PS) on the 531 Newman CAMELS-US basins.
rows.notes: Joint state + precipitation variational data assimilation (δHBV-DA-PS) on 16-bucket δHBV 1.1p from Jamaat et al. (2025, Journal of Hydrology 663, 134137, Table 1, p. 15): optimizes all 5 log-transformed HBV water stores (SNOWPACK, MELTWATER, SM, SUZ, SLZ) at the start of the 5-day assimilation window [t-5, t-1] and the quartic precipitation multiplier k^4 at t-1 via Adadelta (lr=25.9, 5 steps, NSELossBatch3, monotonic acceptance gate) to predict day-t streamflow (indexed as window [t-4, t] predicting day t+1 in Jamaat et al., 2025). Trained on 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 across 531 Newman basins with 3 Daymet forcings (PRCP, T, Hargreaves Ep) and 35 static attributes; evaluated on 1990-10-01 to 1999-09-30 (first test water year 1989–1990 used as 365-day warm-up buffer). Median NSE = 0.82, Median KGE = 0.852, Low-flow RMSE = 0.01 mm/d, High-flow RMSE = 2.66 mm/d.

rows.asterisk_reason: Evaluated on WY1991–1999 (9 water years; 1989–1990 used as 365-day spin-up buffer) in Jamaat et al. (2025).
rows.family_description: 16-bucket differentiable HBV (δHBV 1.1p, with 3 dynamic time-varying parameters predicted by a 256-unit regional LSTM from 3 Daymet meteorological forcings and 35 static catchment attributes) coupled with training-free 5-day sliding-window variational data assimilation (Adadelta, 5 steps per window, NSELossBatch3 with monotonic acceptance gating) that updates initial hydrological log-states (SNOWPACK, MELTWATER, SM, SUZ, SLZ; δHBV-DA-S), last-day precipitation multiplier k^4 (δHBV-DA-P), or both jointly (δHBV-DA-PS) on the 531 Newman CAMELS-US basins.
rows.notes: State-only variational data assimilation (δHBV-DA-S) on 16-bucket δHBV 1.1p from Jamaat et al. (2025, Journal of Hydrology 663, 134137, Table 1, p. 15): optimizes the 5 log-transformed HBV water stores (SNOWPACK, MELTWATER, SM, SUZ, SLZ) at the start of the 5-day assimilation window [t-5, t-1] via Adadelta (lr=25.9, 5 steps, NSELossBatch3, monotonic acceptance gate) to predict day-t streamflow. Trained on 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 across 531 Newman basins with 3 Daymet forcings and 35 static attributes; evaluated on 1990-10-01 to 1999-09-30 (first test water year 1989–1990 used as 365-day warm-up buffer). Median NSE = 0.82, Median KGE = 0.841, Low-flow RMSE = 0.01 mm/d, High-flow RMSE = 2.69 mm/d.

rows.paradigm: Data-Integration LSTM with 1-Day Lagged Streamflow Q(t-1)
rows.family_description: Clean-room PyTorch re-implementation of the Feng et al. (2020) 256-unit Data-Integration LSTM (DI(1)-LSTM) ingesting daily meteorological forcings, standardized 1-day lagged target-basin observed specific discharge Q(t-1) with binary validity indicator, and 27 static catchment attributes, trained with basin-variance-weighted NSE* loss over 365-day sequences across 6 random seeds on the canonical 531-basin Newman Split-1 Gauged protocol (1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 training, 1989-10-01 to 1999-09-30 evaluation).
rows.notes: 6-seed ensemble (seeds 101..106) of our clean-room DI(1)-LSTM implementation (models/feng2020_di_lstm) trained on 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 and evaluated on 1989-10-01 to 1999-09-30 across all 531 CAMELS-US basins using single-forcing NLDAS meteorological inputs plus 1-day lagged observed streamflow Q(t-1) (Ensemble Med NSE = 0.801, Mean NSE = 0.779, Med KGE = 0.798).

rows.paradigm: Data-Integration LSTM with 1-Day Lagged Streamflow Q(t-1)
rows.family_description: Clean-room PyTorch re-implementation of the Feng et al. (2020) 256-unit Data-Integration LSTM (DI(1)-LSTM) ingesting daily meteorological forcings, standardized 1-day lagged target-basin observed specific discharge Q(t-1) with binary validity indicator, and 27 static catchment attributes, trained with basin-variance-weighted NSE* loss over 365-day sequences across 6 random seeds on the canonical 531-basin Newman Split-1 Gauged protocol (1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 training, 1989-10-01 to 1999-09-30 evaluation).
rows.notes: Single-model evaluation scored across all 6 individual seed members (seeds 101..106; evaluation_mode='single_member_mean') of our clean-room DI(1)-LSTM implementation on 1989-10-01 to 1999-09-30 across all 531 CAMELS-US basins using single-forcing NLDAS meteorological inputs plus 1-day lagged observed streamflow Q(t-1) (Single-Seed Med NSE = 0.795 ± 0.002).

rows.asterisk_reason: Evaluated on WY1991–1999 (9 water years; 1989–1990 used as 365-day spin-up buffer) in Jamaat et al. (2025).
rows.family_description: 16-bucket differentiable HBV (δHBV 1.1p, with 3 dynamic time-varying parameters predicted by a 256-unit regional LSTM from 3 Daymet meteorological forcings and 35 static catchment attributes) coupled with training-free 5-day sliding-window variational data assimilation (Adadelta, 5 steps per window, NSELossBatch3 with monotonic acceptance gating) that updates initial hydrological log-states (SNOWPACK, MELTWATER, SM, SUZ, SLZ; δHBV-DA-S), last-day precipitation multiplier k^4 (δHBV-DA-P), or both jointly (δHBV-DA-PS) on the 531 Newman CAMELS-US basins.
rows.notes: Precipitation-only variational data assimilation (δHBV-DA-P) on 16-bucket δHBV 1.1p from Jamaat et al. (2025, Journal of Hydrology 663, 134137, Table 1, p. 15): optimizes a per-basin quartic precipitation multiplier k^4 at the last day t-1 of the 5-day assimilation window [t-5, t-1] via Adadelta (lr=25.9, 5 steps, NSELossBatch3, monotonic acceptance gate) to predict day-t streamflow. Trained on 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 across 531 Newman basins with 3 Daymet forcings and 35 static attributes; evaluated on 1990-10-01 to 1999-09-30 (first test water year 1989–1990 used as 365-day warm-up buffer). Median NSE = 0.74, Median KGE = 0.800, Low-flow RMSE = 0.05 mm/d, High-flow RMSE = 3.15 mm/d.

protocol.benchmark_name: CAMELS-531 Unified Model Intercomparison Project (Newman Period)
protocol.train_period: 1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30 (9 water years, water years 2000–2008; 3,288 daily steps)
protocol.eval_period: 1989-10-01 to 1999-09-30 (10 water years, water years 1990–1999; 3652 daily steps)

spatial_regimes.title: Gauged Simulation
spatial_regimes.description: Temporal split-sample across all 531 CAMELS-US benchmark basins: calibrated/trained on water years 2000–2008 (1999-10-01 to 2008-09-30) and evaluated out-of-sample on water years 1990–1999 (1989-10-01 to 1999-09-30).

spatial_regimes.title: Prediction in Ungauged Basins (12-Fold Random PUB)
spatial_regimes.description: Out-of-sample spatial cross-validation across k = 12 random folds of the 531 basins (44–45 basins/fold), trained on 11 folds during water years 2000–2008 and evaluated on the held-out fold during water years 1990–1999.

spatial_regimes.title: Prediction in Ungauged Regions (18-Fold HUC-02 PUR)
spatial_regimes.description: Zero-shot regional extrapolation across all 18 USGS two-digit HUC-02 hydrologic regions: trained on 17 regions during water years 2000–2008 and evaluated on the held-out HUC-02 region during water years 1990–1999.

forcing_regimes.title: Single CAMELS Forcing
forcing_regimes.description: Models driven by a single standard CAMELS-US meteorological dataset (Daymet, Maurer, or NLDAS) without lagged streamflow inputs.

forcing_regimes.title: Multiple CAMELS Forcings
forcing_regimes.description: Models driven simultaneously by any combination of two or three standard CAMELS-US meteorological datasets (Daymet, Maurer, and/or NLDAS) without lagged streamflow inputs.

forcing_regimes.title: With Lagged Streamflow Inputs
forcing_regimes.description: Models ingesting lagged observed streamflow, autoregression, or data assimilation alongside meteorological forcings (or donor-gauge transfer in PUB/PUR).

forcing_regimes.title: Freeform Forcings (Non-CAMELS Inputs)
forcing_regimes.description: Models driven by non-CAMELS meteorological forcing products (such as AORC, EM-Earth, or ERA5-Land).

provenance_categories.Literature: Skill scores extracted directly from a published paper evaluated on the standard splits.
provenance_categories.Archive: Metrics calculated by the MIP from publicly archived daily hydrographs associated with a prior published paper.
provenance_categories.Archive*: Metrics calculated by the MIP from publicly archived daily hydrographs on a partial basin subset (<531 basins) or non-standard time period.
provenance_categories.MIP Re-run: Published model re-implemented and re-run by the MIP on the standardized 531-basin splits.
provenance_categories.Contribution: New model contributed directly to the MIP benchmark.
